chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about al-fuqqa' (a type of beer/drink), so he said: "It is the wine itself."
278 - From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn al-Qalanisi said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him) asking him about al-fuqqa', so he said: "Do not approach it, for it is from the wine."

key_terms.الْفُقَّاعِ: Fuqqa' (a type of fermented grain drink/beer)
key_terms.لَا تَقْرَبْهُ: Do not approach it (a common fiqh phrase for prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on Fuqqa' (beer) according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) classifies 'al-fuqqa''—a traditional fermented beverage—as 'al-khamrah' (wine) itself, establishing its prohibition based on the principle of *kaffah* (totality of intoxication) rather than just the degree of intoxication. The additional instruction to 'do not approach it' (*la taqrabhu*) highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on preventive caution (*sadr al-dhahab*) regarding fermented drinks, even if they are not fully intoxicating in small quantities. This ruling underscores the broader Quranic prohibition of intoxicants as 'defilement from the work of Satan', extending the concept of wine to include any fermented drink that retains the potential for intoxication.
